READING

**Reframing the comparison**

The problem statement correctly points out that the GBP 27,072 learning-curve remake bill is identical under both courses and can therefore be set aside. The decision rests on three live financial variables — overtime, crossing remakes, and the reputation cost of visible quality deterioration — plus the operational risk of running two parallel systems.

---

**Blended remake rates: what practices actually see**

The pilot measured 11.4 % for the first 300 units and 4.2 % for the next 300. At 646 units a year (≈ 54 units/month), a technician clears the 300-unit threshold around month 5.6 and the 600-unit threshold around month 11. Those numbers frame what each practice observes month by month.

*KIRKBANE — all ten start 2027-01-04*

For the first 5–6 months, all ten transitioning technicians sit at 11.4 %. Blended across twelve benches:

(10 × 11.4 + 2 × 3.4) ÷ 12 ≈ **10.1 %**

That is more than three times the settled rate. Every one of the forty practices sees it at once. The rate only drops sharply — to roughly 4.1 % — when the cohort collectively clears 300 units around mid-2027, and returns to par by December 2027.

*AVENSWOOD — three batches of 3, then 1, across nine months*

| Period | New (phase) | Remaining old | 2 pilot | Blended |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 3 at 11.4 % | 7 at 3.1 % | 3.4 % | **≈ 5.2 %** |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 3 at 11.4 % + 3 at 4.2 % | 4 at 3.1 % | 3.4 % | **≈ 5.5 %** |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 3 at 11.4 % + 3 at 4.2 % + 3 settling | 1 at 3.1 % | 3.4 % | **≈ 7.5 %** |
| Oct–Dec 2027 | 1 at 11.4 % + others graduating | 0 | — | **≈ 6–6.5 %** |

The peak of roughly 7.5 % in mid-2027 is bad, but it is materially lower than KIRKBANE's 10 % opening, and it is diluted across time rather than announced simultaneously to all practices. Three-quarters of the bench is at settled quality from day one; a practice that phones with a query almost always reaches capacity that is not on the steep slope.

---

**Crossing remakes under AVENSWOOD**

The pilot placed 2 technicians on the new system alongside 10 on the old, and recorded 40 crossing remakes in four months. The most natural model for crossing-remake rate is proportional to the product of technicians on each side (new × old), because a crossing remake requires an active hand-off across the boundary in both directions.

Pilot calibration: 2 × 10 = 20 exposure-units over 4 months → 40 remakes → **0.5 remakes per exposure-unit per month.**

AVENSWOOD exposure across three phases (each ≈ 3 months):

| Phase | Split | Exposure-units | Duration | Remakes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan–Apr 2027 | 5 new, 7 old | 35 | 3 months | 52.5 |
| Apr–Jul 2027 | 8 new, 4 old | 32 | 3 months | 48.0 |
| Jul–Oct 2027 | 11 new, 1 old | 11 | 3 months | 16.5 |
| **Total** | | | | **≈ 117** |

At GBP 96 each: **≈ GBP 11,230.**

This estimate is uncertain — better case-routing protocols could halve it; sloppy handovers could push it higher — but it is unlikely to reach GBP 44,000.

Under KIRKBANE, everyone is on the same system from 2027-01-04. Crossing remakes are effectively zero.

---

**Direct financial comparison (excluding the equal learning-curve cost)**

| Item | KIRKBANE | AVENSWOOD |
|---|---|---|
| Overtime | GBP 44,000 | GBP 0 |
| Crossing remakes | GBP 0 | ≈ GBP 11,230 |
| **Net differential** | **GBP 44,000** | **≈ GBP 11,230** |

AVENSWOOD is approximately **GBP 33,000 cheaper** on measurable direct costs.

---

**The dual shade library**

Running two shade libraries for nine months is a genuine risk. Practices receive shade references from the lab's records, and if a case started under one library is matched against the other, the result can be a mismatched restoration — another form of crossing error. Strict protocols (for example, locking completed shade records against the system on which work started) can contain this, but it is not costless to manage. It is worth noting, however, that the pilot measurement of 40 crossing remakes almost certainly already reflects shade-library confusion as part of its cause, since the pilot ran two libraries concurrently. The GBP 11,230 estimate therefore probably absorbs this risk, rather than understating it.

---

**Reputation and practice-retention risk**

Forty practices seeing a 10 % remake rate in the same month under KIRKBANE is the hardest item to price. Each practice that defects as a result of a quality shock costs far more than GBP 33,000 to replace — revenue, relationship rebuild time, and the margin on years of future orders. Even if practices are understanding about a disclosed transition, a simultaneous system-wide deterioration is a compelling reason for procurement managers to look elsewhere. The concentrated, simultaneous nature of KIRKBANE's spike is the item that weighs most heavily against it.

Under AVENSWOOD, the elevated rate is real but diffused. The majority of output is always at settled quality. Practices that do experience above-par remakes are dealing with one or two technicians in transition, not a laboratory-wide crisis.

---

**Deadline check**

The Kessendale support deadline is 2028-06-30. Under AVENSWOOD, the last technician moves to the new system on 2027-10-04 — Kessendale is therefore decommissioned roughly eight months before its support expiry. The fact that this technician completes their learning curve only around September 2028 is irrelevant to the deadline: they are already working on the replacement system. Both courses are comfortably within the deadline.

---

**Summary judgement**

AVENSWOOD is better on every measurable dimension except the dual-library management burden and the crossing-remake count — and both of those disadvantages, totalled, cost roughly a quarter of what KIRKBANE's overtime bill costs. The staggered course also prevents a quality catastrophe visible simultaneously to all forty practices, which is the kind of event that loses accounts permanently. The nine months of parallel-system running is an operational inconvenience that is fully manageable with disciplined case-routing protocols.

READING

CALL
AVENSWOOD

GROUNDS
AVENSWOOD saves roughly GBP 33,000 against KIRKBANE once crossing remakes are set against overtime, and by keeping three-quarters of the bench at the settled rate throughout it avoids the simultaneous ten-per-cent remake-rate shock that KIRKBANE would deliver to all forty practices in the same month — the single outcome most likely to trigger practice defections that no financial calculation could recover.
